subject: Proposal: 9-month term extension + tiered rebate to smooth commit
messages:
From: Sam Walker <sam.walker@fulcrumhealth.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@fulcrumhealth.io>
Date: 2027-08-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation

Thanks for the call this morning, Irene. A couple of points from Fulcrum's side:

- We are comfortable with a 12-month economic window but our CFO prefers a shorter firm term given uncertainty in Q1 next year.
- Volume is likely to ramp in H2 2028 if our pilot converts, but July looked softer than expected (attached csv).

Can Redwood do a 9-month extension on current pricing plus a tiered rebate structure tied to usage milestones? Ideally the rebate would kick in as a credit against the last invoice of the term. Also need clarity on how unused committed capacity rolls forward (or not).

If you can send a concrete term-sheet, we can run it quickly with procurement.

—Sam
Sam Walker
Head of Platform Ops, Fulcrum Health
sam.walker@fulcrumhealth.io

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Walker <sam.walker@fulcrumhealth.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: 9-month term extension + tiered rebate to smooth commit

Sam — thanks for the clear ask and for the usage file. We discussed internally and sketched two pragmatic options that aim to balance your CFO's desire for a shorter firm commitment with Redwood's need for predictability:

1) Term Extension + Tiered Rebate (preferred)
   - 9-month firm extension from 2027-10-01 to 2028-06-30
   - Committed baseline stays at your current monthly commit; overages billed at list
   - If total billed usage during the 9-month term exceeds 110% of commit -> 6% credit applied to final invoice
   - If exceeds 130% -> 12% credit applied to final invoice
   - Any unused committed capacity does NOT roll forward; instead, we offer a one-time conversion credit equal to 20% of the unused commitment value to be used as setup/consulting credit within 6 months

2) Short Firm + True-up Cushion
   - 6-month firm with a 3-month optional extension (mutual opt-in)
   - A usage true-up at contract end with a tiered discount schedule (smaller credits than option 1)

Attached is a draft term_sheet_v2.pdf for option 1 wording and a summary of how credits appear on an invoice.

Next steps: if option 1 looks promising, I can loop in Contracts for a clean amendment and send DocuSign this week so procurement can review. Karthik — any constraints on rebate accounting we should flag? Lauren — happy to run the invoice example for them.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive — Enterprise Renewals
Redwood Inference

Attachments: term_sheet_v2.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Sam Walker <sam.walker@fulcrumhealth.io>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-10T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: 9-month term extension + tiered rebate to smooth commit

Circling on accounting/ops:

- Rebate applied as a contra-invoice credit on the final invoice of the term is cleanest from our billing system standpoint. We should include language that credits are non-refundable and only apply to Redwood invoices.
- For procurement: we can structure the one-time conversion credit as a "service credit" with a 6-month redemption window; that avoids IFRS complications of deferred revenue reversal.
- We should include a clause that if Fulcrum requests a model-variant upgrade (e.g., quantized lower-cost variant) that materially changes unit economics, we re-run rebate thresholds with 30 days' notice.

Irene — happy to review the DocuSign wordings for accounting-specific language.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@fulcrumhealth.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sam Walker <sam.walker@fulcrumhealth.io>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-12T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: 9-month term extension + tiered rebate to smooth commit

Irene/Karthik — thank you. Option 1 looks reasonable to our CFO as long as the 20% conversion credit is clearly restricted to Redwood professional services or onboarding credits (not cash). Two quick clarifications:

1) Can the 6% / 12% rebate bands be applied pro-rata if they hit thresholds mid-term (i.e., prorated credit rather than binary)? Our procurement prefers pro-rata so the credit reflects real consumption.
2) For the unused commitment conversion credit, would Redwood accept that it be used across any Redwood product lines, or does it have to be service-only?

If you can answer those two points and send a final DocuSign, we can route to procurement/finance by EOD Friday.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

—Maya
Maya Patel
Procurement Manager, Fulcrum Health
Attachments: Fulcrum_Usage_Report_Jul2027.csv
